claim.why_it_matters: The PDF prints this as a numbered section heading (bold, own line), like 6.4.2.2 on page 109 which the markdown renders as '###'; here it is left as a plain paragraph, so the section is invisible to heading-based navigation and section lookup.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 110 (II-26) shows '6.4.4 Sharing Files' on its own line as a numbered section heading, the same typewriter style as '6.5 INTRA-PROGRAM COMMUNICATION', '6.5.1 Transfer of Control' and '6.5.2 Shared Data' on the same page. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md (line 4859) and page-110.md it is a plain paragraph, while its sibling '### 6.4.3 Sharing Data' (line 4843) and '### 6.4.2.2 Values of Parameters' are markdown headings. The text is present and correct; the defect is the missing heading markup, which hides the section from heading-based lookup. The claim's 'bold' is inaccurate: the page is uniform typewriter text and the heading is not bold.
verdict.corrected_description: '6.4.4 Sharing Files' is a numbered section heading on its own line in the PDF (typewriter, not bold) but the markdown leaves it as a plain paragraph instead of '### 6.4.4 Sharing Files' like its sibling 6.4.3. The same page's headings 6.5, 6.5.1 and 6.5.2 are also plain paragraphs in the markdown (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md lines 4867, 4871, 4887).
